content.text:
I built the part and exported it to `submission.step`. It's a single solid, and reading the STEP file back gives the same shape.

**The part:** a flat plate shaped like a slice of a disc, lying in the XY plane. The point of the slice is at the origin, the radius is 100, and it covers 0° to 100° measured from +X towards +Y. It's 8 thick, extruded along +Z. That makes the overall size 117.4 × 100 × 8.

**How well it matches (silhouette IoU against `composite.png`):**

| View (camera position) | IoU |
|---|---|
| [1,-1,1] | 0.977 |
| [-1,1,-1] | 0.978 |
| [-1,-1,-1] | 0.873 |
| [1,1,1] | 0.864 |
| **Mean** | **0.923** |

I worked out the 0°–100° range from the slopes of the straight edges in the [1,-1,1] view. A 90° quarter-disc only reached a mean of 0.88, and a range centred on the diagonal (−10° to 100°) did no better.

The two top views score lower probably because the reference image cuts off the left and right ends of the part in those views. That throws off the size alignment, so I didn't try to tune the shape to them. The thickness is an estimate from the images and I didn't fine-tune it.

The part was built with a CadQuery script, so it has no editable feature tree. That doesn't matter for scoring the STEP file.
